analysis_method.batch_rule: Files were sorted by relative path and partitioned into batches of at most 15.
analysis_method.source_analysis: Static AST/source inspection of imports, classes, functions, module variables, state structures, resource paths, protocol handlers, validation logic, tests, and call boundaries.
analysis_method.bytecode_analysis: Static .pyc header, code-object, symbol, constant, and source-correspondence inspection using marshal/code metadata without executing bytecode.

findings: The minimal-controller family uses a thin MCP stdio shell around a stateful Controller object.
Transaction is a dataclass; Controller maintains an in-memory transaction dictionary and persists JSON receipts.
The basic state machine is questions -> answers -> script -> complete.
Validation is exact-schema oriented: response keys are explicitly compared rather than loosely accepted.
Receipt persistence uses temporary-file replacement, giving an atomic-write pattern.
minimal-controller-clone extends the state machine with architecture_choice and solution_application_questions before the ordinary question sequence.
The clone dynamically resolves solver-architecture-kb/scripts/server.py using importlib.util and calls architecture().

The large original execution controller is a deterministic contract/state controller with explicit schemas, protocols, integrity hashes, evidence classification, knowledge retrieval, action authorization, and impasse classification.

bytecode_notes.source_correspondence: Every .pyc in this batch maps to a sibling source file.
bytecode_notes.significance: The stale clone bytecode predates the current architecture-selection additions, preserving an older design state.

findings: runtime_runner.py bridges the deterministic execution-contract controller with runtime_client/carrier state.
Its design includes event reconstruction, recording-backlog handling, controller dispatch, and a carrier-event receipt schema.
The compiled MIS modules reveal the same principal boundaries later visible in source: MISController, retrieval adapter, server integration, solver KB adapter, solver query, and HTTP server.
Several CPython 3.12 caches are older than their present source equivalents, making this batch partly an implementation-history snapshot.
This is a layered architecture: MCP transport -> server integration facade -> MISController -> retrieval abstraction -> SolverKnowledgeAdapter -> solver_query.
RetrievalAdapter is defined as a Protocol, allowing retrieval implementations to be swapped without changing MISController.
RetrievalResult is a dataclass carrying query, matches, status, adapter identity, provenance, and error information.
MISController separates user questions from external evidence acquisition.
Its state machine contains await_q1, questions, await_inquiry_plan, await_evidence, await_script, and complete.
Solver KB records are explicitly designated solver guidance rather than evidence for externally checkable claims.
The same tool implementation is exposed over both stdio MCP and an HTTP MCP server.

bytecode_notes.observation: The older test bytecode still contains an earlier end-to-end protocol test while current source tests separately enforce world-evidence boundaries.

findings: The v1.1 tests encode architectural invariants, not merely unit behavior: KB guidance cannot be world evidence; external evidence must be separated; retrieval occurs before q1.
The original_execution_runtime files in v1.2 are byte-for-byte identical at source level to the copies in the other MIS packages.
That runtime uses integrity-sealed JSON payloads, explicit authority labels, transport protocols, a persistent event model, and a deterministic/semantic split.
Its operation taxonomy includes READ, SEARCH, CALCULATE, TRANSFORM, MUTATE, CREATE, DELETE, SEND, EXECUTE, WAIT, and OTHER.
v1.2 preserves the controller/retrieval/server layering of v1.1.
The major retrieval change is rank_all_knowledge(): every selected canonical KB record is returned in deterministic k-descending/id-ascending order rather than only a top-k subset.
Ranking uses BM25-style token scoring, exact ID/alias boosts, type priors, and separately reported one-hop link influence.
SolverKnowledgeAdapter converts ranked KB records into normalized RetrievalResult matches with explicit rank, k, score components, link provenance, and epistemic role.
retrieve_context becomes a complete-KB ranking interface rather than a small top-k lookup.
The HTTP server health response explicitly identifies version 1.2.0, HTTP transport, and /mcp.

bytecode_notes.observation: The older solver_query bytecode does not contain _score_records/rank_all_knowledge, confirming that complete-KB ranking was added after that cache was produced.

findings: v1.2 explicitly tests parity across HTTP and stdio surfaces.
The tests assert that complete KB ranking contains every record sorted by k.
The stdio server remains a thin newline-delimited JSON-RPC adapter over the same TOOLS/call_tool implementation used by HTTP.
The base MIS package again contains the identical original execution runtime, demonstrating vendored duplication rather than shared-package dependency.
The base MIS version shows the earlier architecture from which v1.1 evolved.
Its MISController has retrieval -> q1/questions -> script, without the later inquiry_plan/external_evidence phases.
The same retrieval abstraction and integration facade already exist, showing that v1.1 extended the controller state machine rather than replacing the overall architecture.
The original execution runtime runner remains a separate controller/carrier subsystem rather than being directly embedded into MCP dispatch.

bytecode_notes.observation: The caches in this batch correspond to their present source sizes.

findings: Base MIS tests validate retrieval-before-question behavior and stdio MCP initialization/list/call behavior.
semantic-runtime introduces a different architecture: one transaction-oriented MCP surface backed by tokenized continuation addresses and terminal delivery.
semantic-runtime/http_server is not merely /mcp; it also exposes resolution, acknowledgement, and terminal-delivery operations around the same underlying runtime.
The semantic HTTP layer separates JSON-RPC errors from HTTP transport mechanics and delegates actual state transitions to Runner/DeliveryLedger.
Semantic Runtime represents execution position as self-contained encoded addresses rather than a conventional server-side transaction object.
Runner resolves an alias or token, optionally advances one transition, renders the new screen, and returns a continuation token.
DeliveryLedger adds replay-until-acknowledged semantics around addresses.
DeliveryLedger uses a threading.Lock, pending map, consumed-address set, acknowledged-delivery set, and terminal-to-address map.
Addresses become one-use only after acknowledgement; before acknowledgement the same pending result can be replayed.
coordination_gate is an interception layer around ordinary Runner transitions, providing HOLD/wait behavior without rewriting the core runner.

bytecode_notes.observation: The CPython 3.14 runtime caches correspond to the current source modules.

findings: DefinitionStore makes runtime behavior data-driven: aliases, immutable versioned scripts, and terminal mappings are ordinary JSON definitions.
Script versions are treated as immutable; an existing version may only be delivered again if identical.
token_codec encodes the full continuation state using compact URL-safe base64 JSON.
script_validation implements graph-level checks such as reachability to success, valid screen references, and path correctness.
script_builder is itself a runtime handler/state machine for constructing and publishing new scripts.
sheet_push provides an external delivery adapter to Apps Script.
semantic-runtime/server.py exposes exactly one MCP tool, transaction, despite the much larger internal runtime.
The MCP tool can operate locally or delegate statelessly to a configured Apps Script endpoint.
Tests target immutable versions, resumable tokens, failed-write retry behavior, HTTP acknowledgement semantics, and stdio MCP behavior.
solver-architecture-kb is a compact HTTP MCP server implemented entirely with the Python standard library.
Its data layer is knowledge.jsonl plus ontology.json.
Retrieval uses token counters and TF-IDF-like cosine similarity.
classify() applies cue-based labels across ontology perspectives and marks unsupported dimensions needs-evidence.
architecture() combines classification with retrieved analogies and emits candidate architectures, selected stages, deterministic operations, semantic operations, coverage gaps, and stop conditions.
ingest_knowledge mutates the JSONL corpus and deterministically derives an ID from the record when one is absent.
configure_tunnel.py is a small configuration writer that requires an HTTPS tunnel URL.

cross_batch_patterns.pattern: Thin MCP adapter over a separate implementation layer
cross_batch_patterns.source_observation: server.py/stdio_server.py/http_server.py files largely implement initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call, serialization, and errors, while Controller, MISController, Runner, retrieval adapters, or KB functions perform domain work.

Controller.phase, Tx.phase, Runner screen addresses, execution-contract predicate state, and builder phases all encode finite execution states explicitly rather than relying on conversational inference.
Tools carry JSON inputSchema definitions; controller prompts carry return_schema objects; many response handlers require exact keys and types.
Several systems expose the same implementation through stdio and HTTP without duplicating domain logic.
MCP call results commonly return both serialized text content and structuredContent.
Minimal Controller, MISController, Execution Contract Controller, and Semantic Runtime all preserve explicit execution/event state in some form.
State advancement is guarded by exact schema checks, transition membership, allowed enums, graph validation, or evidence/accounting checks.

Solver behavior is substantially driven by JSON/JSONL KB records, ontology definitions, alias definitions, versioned scripts, terminal definitions, or return-schema objects rather than hard-coded monolithic flows.
RetrievalAdapter/NullRetrievalAdapter/SolverKnowledgeAdapter and Semantic Runtime's delivery/push layers isolate optional external mechanisms.

cross_batch_patterns.pattern: Boundary between deterministic and semantic work
cross_batch_patterns.source_observation: The execution-contract runtime explicitly distinguishes deterministic actions/procedures from semantic requests; solver-architecture similarly labels deterministic_operations and semantic_operations.
MIS v1.1/v1.2 treats KB records as solver guidance and explicitly prevents them from being submitted as world evidence.
Atomic receipt replacement, immutable script publishing, replay-until-acknowledged delivery, deterministic hashes, and retry tests recur across implementations.
controller, CONTROLLER, RETRIEVAL_SERVICE, RUNNER, DELIVERIES, and TERMINAL_STATE are module-level process objects.
cross_batch_patterns.inference: These designs favor simple single-process service operation. In-memory state such as active transactions or terminal state does not itself imply restart persistence.

notable_functions_and_variables.role: Newline-delimited JSON-RPC/MCP framing and tool dispatch.
Adds architecture retrieval/selection as a prerequisite to domain interrogation.
State machine that separates solver guidance, user-provided information, external evidence, and executable procedure generation.
Deterministic lexical/BM25-style ranking and normalized retrieval.
Formal controller alternating deterministic protocol/state enforcement with explicitly requested semantic decisions.
Token-addressed finite-state execution and terminal delivery engine behind a single MCP tool.
Ontology-guided architecture retrieval/synthesis exposed as HTTP MCP.

local_dependency_chains: semantic-runtime/server.py -> Runner + DefinitionStore + DeliveryLedger + sheet_push -> runtime modules
resource_dependencies: Execution runtime: execution_knowledge_base.json plus runtime manifest/state/overlay/event files
Solver Architecture KB: data/knowledge.jsonl and assets/ontology.json
external_service_edges: Semantic Runtime optionally posts to Google Apps Script.
Semantic Runtime terminal metadata constructs Google Sheets URLs.
Solver Architecture KB and MIS v1.2 can be exposed through an HTTP/tunnel configuration.

versioning_and_duplication.important_conclusion: The .pyc set is useful both as compiled confirmation of source structure and as implementation-history evidence, but it must not be assumed that every .pyc represents the current adjacent .py.

major_duplicate_family.observation: These four source files are byte-for-byte identical across mis-solver-query, mis-solver-query-v1-1, and mis-solver-query-v1-2.

evolution: Base MIS: retrieval -> user q1 -> script.
MIS v1.1: adds explicit inquiry planning and external-evidence acquisition, and prohibits solver-KB guidance from masquerading as world evidence.
MIS v1.2: retains the v1.1 state machine but changes retrieval toward complete canonical-KB ranking using rank_all_knowledge and adds HTTP-specific validation/tests.
minimal-controller-clone: evolves the minimal controller by inserting solver-architecture selection and application-specific questioning.
Semantic Runtime: represents a separate design lineage emphasizing tokenized continuation state, immutable data-defined scripts, single-tool MCP exposure, and acknowledged delivery.

mcp_architecture_findings.finding: The irreducible protocol shell is small.
mcp_architecture_findings.details: Across these servers, the recurring MCP core is initialize + ping + tools/list + tools/call + JSON-RPC result/error framing. Domain complexity is optional and sits behind that boundary.
TOOLS lists or TRANSACTION_TOOL dictionaries define name, description, and inputSchema separately from the dispatch implementation.

mcp_architecture_findings.finding: One MCP endpoint can hide a large runtime.
mcp_architecture_findings.details: semantic-runtime exposes only transaction while internally containing routing, continuation tokens, graph validation, script construction, delivery acknowledgement, terminal state, and Apps Script integration.

mcp_architecture_findings.finding: stdio and HTTP are interchangeable outer transports in these designs.
mcp_architecture_findings.details: MIS exposes the same call_tool/TOOLS domain surface through stdio_server.py and scripts/server.py.

mcp_architecture_findings.finding: The most reusable MCP boundary is transport -> tool registry -> dispatcher -> domain function.
mcp_architecture_findings.details: This pattern appears in minimal-controller, MIS, semantic-runtime, and solver-architecture-kb with different amounts of machinery behind the domain function.

mcp_architecture_findings.finding: State does not need to live in the MCP protocol layer.
mcp_architecture_findings.details: State is delegated to Controller/Tx objects, encoded continuation tokens, definition files, delivery ledgers, or formal controller payloads.

mcp_architecture_findings.finding: Exact structured contracts are favored over free-form messages.
mcp_architecture_findings.details: The code repeatedly validates exact keys, required properties, enums, IDs, state transitions, evidence accounting, and graph structure before accepting a transition.

mcp_architecture_findings.finding: The examined implementations require no third-party MCP SDK.
mcp_architecture_findings.details: The MCP protocol is implemented directly using Python standard-library JSON, stdin/stdout, and http.server primitives.
